newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee exports rise 47 pct in Oct from Sept.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee exports rise 47 pct in Oct from Sept.

text.p: Exports of coffee beans and soluble coffee surged 47 percent in October over September, up to 125,000 tonnes from 85,000 tonnes, the Ministry of Industry and Commerce said.
The ministry said in a statement that receipts from coffee exports totalled $285 million in October, $90 million more than in the previous month.
It did not give quantities in terms of 60-kg bags.
Secretary of Foreign Trade Mauricio Cortes told reporters that in comparison with October 1995, coffee prices were 15.86 percent lower but shipments were up 92.5 percent.
Other sectors said to be performing well were manufactured exports, which expanded 3.0 percent in October from September to $2.268 billion.

Agricultural machinery sales, mainly to the Mercosur countries, rose 92.7 percent, shipments of computer hardware, mainly to the United States and Argentina, increased 42.4 percent and exports of orange juice rose 30.91 percent.
Lower exports were registered in transport goods, with sales of cars, trucks and airplanes falling 17.41 percent while soybean exports dropped 18.66 percent in October over September.
